messages:
maria: Heads-up — CI canary apply for eu-gpu-pool failed with a weird state/lock mismatch error.
cheng: Saw the alert. TF said no lock held but resources exist in eu account.
sam: I ran an import yesterday for a subset, could that have left a half-write? `terraform import module.gpu_pool.aws_instance.pool[0]`
maria: Not from my side. ops-bot: DynamoDB lease extended by 600s for run 2143658700.
alex: Quick check — looks like the backend move started (s3 -> archive bucket) and gitops triggered a sync during propagation. Two writers hit the statefile.
cheng: Error snippet: ```Error: State backend mismatch: attempted write to bucket 'redwood-tfstate-eu' but current state file references 'redwood-eu-archive'```
sam: That explains the split. Lock fencing didn't catch it, probably due to a TTL race.
alex: I inspected TTLs — some leases have future expiry because of clock skew on a helper lambda (~+4m). That allowed another apply to acquire a perceived free lease.
maria: Proposed immediate steps: 1) pause infra gitops sync for region eu, 2) put canary provisioning on hold, 3) request oncall approval to force-unlock stale leases, 4) run state reconcile to stitch duplicates.
sam: +1 on pausing. Also we should avoid draining any pools until we confirm which state is canonical.
cheng: I can prepare an unlock script but need an approval window. Tagging @oncall-eng for that.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0422 (auto), notifying #incidents.
oncall-eng: Ack. Hold all infra syncs for eu. Maria — upload the plan and the failing logs.
maria: Uploaded plan and logs to s3://redwood-infra-debug/plans/2143658700-plan.txt
sam: After unlock we should run `terraform state pull` from both buckets and do a diff, then `terraform state rm` on duplicates before reapplying.
alex: Cost note: some partial instances spun for ~3h before we killed them — ~120 USD impact for the window. Will track in the incident.
cheng: Long-term action: add a pre-apply backend-identity check (fail apply if backend UUID mismatch) and a stricter clock drift monitoring for lock renewers.
maria: Also disable auto-import hooks during backend migrations. That would have prevented this accidental partial import.
oncall-eng: Approved. Window open for manual unlock and reconcile (15m). :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary rollback triggered to dedicated eu pool.
sam: Performed force unlock, pulled states, reconciler running. Commands used: ```aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S":"eu-gpu-pool"}}'```
ops-bot: Reconciler completed: success — stitched 1 resource, removed duplicate state keys.
maria: Verified cluster state, terminated orphaned instances, and re-enabled gitops for infra/regions with auto-sync off.
ach: closing note: follow-up ticket opened: INFRA-4539 backend-migration-safety (add pre-checks + clock drift alarms).
maria: resolved. :white_check_mark:
